newsitem.title: USA: Retailer faces long road out of bankruptcy.
newsitem.headline: Retailer faces long road out of bankruptcy.

text.p: Bankrupt retailer Barney's Inc. finally has chosen a partner to help regain its financial footing, but other potential suitors could still emerge to challenge the transaction that will take months to complete.

The long-troubled retailer on Sunday announced it had struck a preliminary pact with Dickson Concepts Ltd. in a deal that will give the Hong Kong firm control of the New York-based family-run company.
But because Barney's is in bankruptcy, the deal faces a long list of court-imposed deadlines before it is finalised.
Two sources familiar with the plan on Monday speculated the deal may not be finalised until next year, leaving plenty of time for other interested parties to jump into the fray.
Barney's has been in bankruptcy since January 1996 and several companies have expressed interest in buying the upscale retailer.

"In the Chapter 11 (bankruptcy) process, there's always an opportunity to be a successful bidder for a company even if someone else looks like they have the best bid," said Damien Kovary, managing director at Heico Acquisitions, a private investment firm that submitted a bid for Barney's.

Kovary did not discount a potential bid for Barney's at a later time, saying "we will continue to remain interested. We will watch the process as it moves forward." He declined to identify the size of the bid submitted.
Texas Pacific Group, another private investment firm that reportedly bid for Barney's, declined to comment.
Meanwhile, Saks Holdings Inc., which recently withdrew from the bidding process after deciding it could not justify its $290 million offer, previously has said it remains interested in Barney's.
A spokeswoman for Saks declined to comment on Monday.
The agreement with Dickson calls for the Hong Kong retailer to pay creditors $205 million in cash, a $42 million note and 49 percent of Barneys' equity in exchange for control of the retailer.

The deal is aimed at saving the upscale retailer, which recently announced it would close several underperforming stores, including its famed Manhattan flagship location. It has been in bankruptcy since January 1996.
The company's exclusive right to file a reorganization plan with the bankruptcy court is is set to expire on Sept. 12, but the retailer is expected to seek an extension as it has done previously.
Once Barney's files a reorganization plan, which would outline the agreement struck with Dickson, other parties may also file proposals.

Founded in 1923 by Barney Pressman and operated by grandsons Robert and Gene, the company has foundered in recent years and has been plagued by a reputation for weak management while it poured money into expansion.
Executives of the company were not available to discuss the preliminary transaction with Dickson.
